They were even more astonished and said to one another, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them and said, "With men it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God."
Peter began to say to Him, "We have left everything and followed You."
Jesus said, "Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for My sake and for the gospel's,
who will not receive a hundred times as much now in this time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions, and in the age to come eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first."
The Third Foretelling

They were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them; they were amazed, and those who followed were afraid. He took the twelve aside again and began to tell them what was going to happen to Him:
"We are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes; they will condemn Him to death and hand Him over to the Gentiles.
They will mock Him and spit on Him, flog Him and kill Him; and after three days He will rise."
James and John
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Him and said, "Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask You."
He said to them, "What do you want Me to do for you?"
They said to Him, "Grant us to sit, one at Your right hand and one at Your left, in Your glory."
Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"
They said to Him, "We can." Jesus said to them, "The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized;
but to sit at My right hand or at My left is not Mine to give; it is for those for whom it has been prepared."
When the ten heard it, they began to be indignant with James and John.
Jesus called them to Him and said to them, "You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great men exercise authority over them.
It shall not be so among you. Whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you shall be slave of all.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many."
Bartimaeus
They came to Jericho. As He was going out of Jericho with His disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the road.
When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out and say, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"
Many rebuked him, telling him to be quiet; but he cried out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and said, "Call him." They called the blind man, saying to him, "Take heart; get up, He is calling you."
Throwing off his cloak, he sprang up and came to Jesus.
Jesus said to him, "What do you want Me to do for you?" The blind man said to Him, "Rabbouni, let me see again."
Jesus said to him, "Go; your faith has made you well." At once he received his sight, and followed Him on the way.

chapters.title: A House of Prayer
chapters.html:
Mark 11

The Coming King

1When they drew near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples

2and said to them, "Go into the village ahead of you, and at once as you enter it you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.

3If anyone says to you, 'Why are you doing this?' say, 'The Lord needs it, and will send it back here at once.'"

4They went away and found a colt tied at a door, outside in the street, and they untied it.

5Some of those standing there said to them, "What are you doing, untying the colt?"

6They spoke to them as Jesus had told them, and they let them go.

7They brought the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks on it, and He sat on it.

8Many spread their cloaks on the road, and others spread leafy branches that they had cut in the fields.

9Those who went ahead and those who followed were shouting, "Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!

10Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!"

11He entered Jerusalem and went into the temple; and when He had looked around at everything, since it was already late, He went out to Bethany with the twelve.

The Fig Tree and the Temple

12The next day, as they were coming from Bethany, He was hungry.

13Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, He went to see whether He might find anything on it. When He came to it, He found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.

14He said to it, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again." His disciples were listening.

15They came to Jerusalem. He entered the temple and began to drive out those who were selling and buying in the temple, and He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who sold doves.

16He would not let anyone carry anything through the temple.

17He was teaching and saying to them, "Is it not written, 'My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations'? But you have made it a den of robbers."

18The chief priests and the scribes heard it and began looking for a way to destroy Him; for they were afraid of Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching.

19When evening came, they went out of the city.

20As they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.

21Peter remembered and said to Him, "Rabbi, look! The fig tree that You cursed has withered."

22Jesus answered them, "Have faith in God.

23Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says will happen, it will be done for him.

24That is why I tell you, all that you pray and ask for, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.

25Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses."

By What Authority?

27They came again to Jerusalem. As He was walking in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders came to Him

28and said to Him, "By what authority are You doing these things? Or who gave You this authority to do them?"

29Jesus said to them, "I will ask you one question; answer Me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

30The baptism of John: was it from heaven, or from men? Answer Me."

31They discussed it among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Why then did you not believe him?'

32But shall we say, 'From men'?" — they were afraid of the crowd, for everyone held that John really was a prophet.

33So they answered Jesus, "We do not know." Jesus said to them, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."

Notes

  • vv1–7 "a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat… The Lord needs it" — the king of Zechariah 9:9, riding on a donkey, on a colt, comes from the Mount of Olives, where the LORD's feet will stand (Zechariah 14:4). An animal never used was set apart for holy use, as the red heifer on which a yoke has never come (Numbers 19:2).

  • vv8–10 "spread their cloaks on the road… Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!" — the people spread garments for Jehu when he was made king, every man took his garment and put it under him (2 Kings 9:13). Hōsanna is the Hebrew hoshi'a na, save, please, the cry of Psalm 118:25, Please, LORD, save us!, and the next verse follows, Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD! (Psalm 118:26). Mark adds the coming kingdom of our father David.

  • vv12–14, 20–21 "a fig tree in leaf… nothing but leaves… withered from the roots" — the prophets use the fig tree for Israel when no fruit is found, no figs on the fig tree, and the leaf has withered (Jeremiah 8:13), and no first-ripe fig that my soul desires (Micah 7:1). Mark sets the temple between the cursing and the withering, so that each explains the other. For it was not the season for figs: the tree's leaves promised what its season could not yet give.

  • vv15–17 "a house of prayer for all the nations… a den of robbers" — two prophets joined: Isaiah, My house will be called a house of prayer for all the peoples (Isaiah 56:7), and Jeremiah, Has this house… become a den of robbers in your eyes? (Jeremiah 7:11). Only Mark has for all the nations, and only Mark has v16. Lēstēs, robber, a bandit, the word used of those crucified with Jesus (15:27).

  • vv22–25 "Have faith in God… this mountain… forgive" — pistin theou, faith in God, word for word faith of God. This mountain: they are on the road from the Mount of Olives (v1), in sight of the temple mount. v26 is not in the edition, so the numbering here skips from 25 to 27.

  • vv27–33 "By what authority… The baptism of John: was it from heaven, or from men?" — exousia, authority, the word of 1:22 and 2:10. Ex ouranou, from heaven, is a way of saying from God.

chapters.title: The Great Commandment
chapters.html:
Mark 12

The Tenants of the Vineyard

1He began to speak to them in parables: "A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a pit for the winepress and built a tower. Then he leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad.

2At the season he sent a slave to the tenants, to receive from them his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

3But they took him, beat him and sent him away empty.

4Again he sent another slave to them; that one they struck on the head and treated shamefully.

5He sent another, and that one they killed; and so with many others, beating some and killing others.

6He still had one, a beloved son. He sent him last of all to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'

7But those tenants said to one another, 'This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'

8They took him, killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.

9What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenants, and give the vineyard to others.

10Have you not read this Scripture: 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner;

11this was from the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes'?"

12They wanted to arrest Him, but they feared the crowd, for they knew He had told the parable against them. So they left Him and went away.

Caesar's and God's

13They sent to Him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to trap Him in what He said.

14They came and said to Him, "Teacher, we know that You are truthful and do not court anyone's favor, for You do not look at the face of men, but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful to pay the tax to Caesar, or not? Should we pay, or should we not?"

15But knowing their hypocrisy, He said to them, "Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to look at."

16They brought one. He said to them, "Whose image is this, and whose inscription?" They said to Him, "Caesar's."

17Jesus said to them, "Give back to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's." They were utterly amazed at Him.

The God of the Living

18Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him and asked Him,

19"Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, his brother shall take the wife and raise up seed for his brother.

20There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and when he died he left no seed.

21The second took her and died, leaving no seed; and the third likewise.

22None of the seven left seed. Last of all the woman also died.

23In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife."

24Jesus said to them, "Is this not why you are going astray, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?

25For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.

26As for the dead being raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the passage about the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'?

27He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are badly astray."

The First Commandment

28One of the scribes came up and heard them arguing, and seeing that He had answered them well, he asked Him, "Which commandment is the first of all?"

29Jesus answered, "The first is: 'Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one;

30and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.'

31The second is this: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' There is no other commandment greater than these."

32The scribe said to Him, "Well said, Teacher; You have spoken the truth, that He is one, and there is no other but Him;

33and to love Him with all the heart and with all the understanding and with all the strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is much more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices."

34When Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, He said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." After that no one dared to ask Him any more questions.

David's Son and David's Lord

35As Jesus was teaching in the temple, He said, "How can the scribes say that the Messiah is the son of David?

36David himself said by the Holy Spirit, 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.'

37David himself calls Him Lord; so how is He his son?" The great crowd listened to Him gladly.

38In His teaching He said, "Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes and to be greeted in the marketplaces,

39and to have the best seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at dinners.

40They devour widows' houses and for show make long prayers. They will receive the greater condemnation."

The Widow's Offering

41He sat down opposite the treasury and watched how the crowd put money into the treasury. Many rich people put in large sums.

42A poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, which make a quadrans.

43He called His disciples to Him and said to them, "Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those who are putting into the treasury.

44For they all put in out of their abundance; but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had, all she had to live on."

Notes

  • vv1–9 "A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a pit for the winepress and built a tower… a beloved son" — Isaiah's song of the vineyard, he built a watchtower in the middle of it, and also hewed out a winepress in it (Isaiah 5:2), where the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel (Isaiah 5:7). Hyion agapēton, a beloved son, the words of the voice at the baptism (1:11) and on the mountain (9:7). Ekephaliōsan, struck on the head.

  • vv10–11 "The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner" — Psalm 118:22–23 in the Greek's words, as Matthew 21:42; the Hebrew has This is the LORD's doing; it is marvelous in our eyes. The rejected son of the parable becomes the stone. Apedokimasan, rejected, the verb of 8:31.

  • vv13–17 "Is it lawful to pay the tax to Caesar… Whose image is this… to God the things that are God's" — kēnsos, tax, a word borrowed from Latin. Eikōn, image: the coin bears Caesar's image, and man was made in the image of God (Genesis 1:27). Apodote, give back: what bears a mark belongs to its owner.

  • vv18–27 "raise up seed for his brother… like angels in heaven… the God of Abraham… not the God of the dead" — the law of the brother-in-law, Her husband's brother shall go in to her (Deuteronomy 25:5). The words at the bush, I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob (Exodus 3:6): God speaks of the patriarchs long dead as His, so they live to Him. Epi tou batou, at the passage about the bush: the section of Exodus is named by its story.

  • vv28–34 "Hear, Israel… the Lord is one… love your neighbor as yourself… more than all whole burnt offerings" — the Shema, Hear, Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4), with all your mind added to the three of Deuteronomy 6:5. The second is Leviticus 19:18. Only Mark has the Shema in this answer and the scribe's reply. The scribe's words are Samuel's and Hosea's, To listen is better than sacrifice (1 Samuel 15:22), and For I desire loyal love and not sacrifice (Hosea 6:6).

  • vv35–37 "The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand" — Psalm 110:1, The LORD says to my lord; in Greek both are kyrios. If David calls the Messiah Lord, He is more than David's son.

  • vv41–44 "two small copper coins, which make a quadrans… all she had to live on" — lepta, the smallest copper coins; kodrantēs, quadrans, a word borrowed from Latin; Mark gives the value. Holon ton bion autēs, all she had to live on, word for word her whole life. Set after the scribes who devour widows' houses (v40).

chapters.title: Keep Awake
chapters.html:
Mark 13

Not One Stone on Another

1As He was going out of the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, "Teacher, look at these great stones and these great buildings!"

2Jesus said to him, "Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be thrown down."

3As He was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked Him privately,

4"Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be accomplished?"

The Beginning of Birth Pains

5Jesus began to say to them, "See that no one leads you astray.

6Many will come in My name, saying, 'I am He,' and they will lead many astray.

7When you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed; these things must happen, but it is not yet the end.

8For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in various places; there will be famines. These are the beginning of birth pains.

9"But watch yourselves. They will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues, and you will stand before governors and kings for My sake, as a testimony to them.

10First the good news must be preached to all the nations.

11When they lead you away and hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what to say, but say whatever is given you in that hour; for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.

12Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise up against parents and have them put to death.

13You will be hated by all because of My name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved.

The Abomination of Desolation

14"When you see the abomination of desolation standing where it ought not to be — let the reader understand — then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

15Let the one on the housetop not go down or go in to take anything out of his house,

16and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.

17Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!

18Pray that it may not happen in winter.

19For in those days there will be affliction such as has not been from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and never will be.

20If the Lord had not cut short those days, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the chosen, whom He chose, He has cut short the days.

21Then if anyone says to you, 'Here is the Messiah!' or 'There He is!' do not believe it.

22For false messiahs and false prophets will arise and perform signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.

23But you, watch; I have told you everything beforehand.

The Coming of the Son of Man

24"But in those days, after that affliction, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light,

25and the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.

26Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

27Then He will send out the angels and gather His chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.

28"Learn the parable from the fig tree: as soon as its branch becomes tender and puts out its leaves, you know that summer is near.

29So also you, when you see these things happening, know that He is near, at the doors.

30Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.

31Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.

No One Knows the Hour

32"But about that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father.

33Watch, stay alert; for you do not know when the time will come.

34It is like a man going on a journey, who leaves his house and puts his slaves in charge, each with his work, and orders the doorkeeper to keep awake.

35Keep awake, then, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming, in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or in the morning;

36otherwise he may come suddenly and find you asleep.

37What I say to you I say to all: keep awake."

Notes

  • vv1–4 "these great stones… Not one stone will be left here on another… on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple" — potapoi, what great, the disciples' wonder. Jesus sits on the Mount of Olives, facing the temple, where the LORD's feet were to stand on His day (Zechariah 14:4). Four disciples ask, the first four called (1:16–20).

  • vv5–8 "I am He… wars and reports of wars… the beginning of birth pains" — Egō eimi, I am He, the words of 6:50; Matthew has I am the Messiah (Matthew 24:5). Ōdinōn, birth pains, the pains of a woman in labor, which end in a birth.

  • vv9–13 "councils… governors and kings… First the good news must be preached to all the nations… the Holy Spirit" — synedria, councils, local courts. Dei, must, the word of 8:31. Hypomeinas eis telos, the one who endures to the end, as Matthew 24:13.

  • vv14–23 "the abomination of desolation standing where it ought not to be… affliction such as has not been" — to bdelygma tēs erēmōseōs, Daniel's loathsome thing that desolates (Daniel 11:31; the note on Matthew 24:15). Hestēkota, standing, is masculine in Greek, where bdelygma is neuter: the thing is spoken of as a person. Let the reader understand, the words to the one who reads. The affliction is Daniel's, a time of distress such as has not been since there was a nation (Daniel 12:1). Ekolobōsen, cut short, the days shortened for the chosen.

  • vv24–27 "the sun will be darkened… coming in clouds with great power and glory… from the four winds" — the prophets' signs of the day of the LORD, the sun will be dark at its rising, and the moon will not shine its light (Isaiah 13:10), and the skies roll up like a scroll (Isaiah 34:4). The coming in clouds is Daniel's, with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man (Daniel 7:13). The gathering is the law's promise, If your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you (Deuteronomy 30:4).

  • vv28–31 "the fig tree… this generation will not pass away… My words will never pass away" — the fig tree of 11:13, now in leaf with summer near. Hē genea hautē, this generation, the word of 8:12, 38 and 9:19.

  • vv32–37 "nor the Son, but the Father… in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or in the morning… keep awake" — the Son does not know the day, as Matthew 24:36 also says. speech.text: Mark 13
Not One Stone on Another
As He was going out of the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, "Teacher, look at these great stones and these great buildings!"
Jesus said to him, "Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be thrown down."
As He was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked Him privately,
"Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be accomplished?"
The Beginning of Birth Pains
Jesus began to say to them, "See that no one leads you astray.
Many will come in My name, saying, 'I am He,' and they will lead many astray.
When you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed; these things must happen, but it is not yet the end.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in various places; there will be famines. These are the beginning of birth pains.
"But watch yourselves. They will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues, and you will stand before governors and kings for My sake, as a testimony to them.
First the good news must be preached to all the nations.
When they lead you away and hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what to say, but say whatever is given you in that hour; for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise up against parents and have them put to death.
You will be hated by all because of My name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
The Abomination of Desolation
"When you see the abomination of desolation standing where it ought not to be — let the reader understand — then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
Let the one on the housetop not go down or go in to take anything out of his house,
and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.

Pray that it may not happen in winter.
For in those days there will be affliction such as has not been from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and never will be.
If the Lord had not cut short those days, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the chosen, whom He chose, He has cut short the days.
Then if anyone says to you, 'Here is the Messiah!' or 'There He is!' do not believe it.
For false messiahs and false prophets will arise and perform signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.
But you, watch; I have told you everything beforehand.
The Coming of the Son of Man
"But in those days, after that affliction, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light,
and the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
Then He will send out the angels and gather His chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
"Learn the parable from the fig tree: as soon as its branch becomes tender and puts out its leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see these things happening, know that He is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.
No One Knows the Hour
"But about that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father.
Watch, stay alert; for you do not know when the time will come.
It is like a man going on a journey, who leaves his house and puts his slaves in charge, each with his work, and orders the doorkeeper to keep awake.
Keep awake, then, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming, in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or in the morning;
otherwise he may come suddenly and find you asleep.
What I say to you I say to all: keep awake."

chapters.title: This Is My Body
chapters.html:
Mark 14

The Anointing at Bethany

1It was two days before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to arrest Him by deceit and kill Him;

2for they said, "Not during the feast, or there may be an uproar among the people."

3While He was at Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, reclining at table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of perfume, pure nard, very costly. She broke the jar and poured it on His head.

4Some there were indignant and said to one another, "Why was the perfume wasted like this?

5This perfume could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor." They scolded her.

6But Jesus said, "Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a beautiful thing to Me.

7For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want you can do good to them; but you do not always have Me.

8She did what she could; she has anointed My body beforehand for burial.

9Truly I tell you, wherever the good news is preached in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her."

10Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to hand Him over to them.

11When they heard it, they were glad and promised to give him money. He began looking for an opportunity to hand Him over.

The Passover Meal

12On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover lamb, His disciples said to Him, "Where do You want us to go and prepare for You to eat the Passover?"

13He sent two of His disciples and said to them, "Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him,

14and wherever he goes in, say to the master of the house, 'The Teacher says, Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?'

15He will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready; prepare for us there."

16The disciples went out and came to the city and found it as He had told them, and they prepared the Passover.

17When evening came, He came with the twelve.

18As they were reclining at table and eating, Jesus said, "Truly I tell you, one of you will hand Me over, one who is eating with Me."

19They began to be grieved and to say to Him one by one, "Surely not I?"

20He said to them, "It is one of the twelve, one who is dipping bread into the bowl with Me.

21The Son of Man goes as it is written of Him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born."

22As they were eating, He took bread, and after saying the blessing He broke it, gave it to them and said, "Take; this is My body."

23He took a cup, and after giving thanks He gave it to them, and they all drank from it.

24He said to them, "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

25Truly I tell you, I will never again drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."

26When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

27Jesus said to them, "You will all fall away; for it is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'

28But after I have been raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."

29Peter said to Him, "Even if all fall away, I will not."

30Jesus said to him, "Truly I tell you, today, this very night, before a rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times."

31But he kept saying vehemently, "Even if I must die with You, I will not deny You." All of them said the same.

Gethsemane

32They came to a place called Gethsemane, and He said to His disciples, "Sit here while I pray."

33He took with Him Peter and James and John, and He began to be greatly distressed and troubled.

34He said to them, "My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Stay here and keep awake."

35Going a little farther, He fell on the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from Him.

36He said, "Abba, Father, all things are possible for You. Take this cup away from Me; yet not what I will, but what You will."

37He came and found them sleeping, and He said to Peter, "Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep awake one hour?

38Keep awake and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak."

39Again He went away and prayed, saying the same words.

40Again He came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy; and they did not know what to answer Him.

41He came a third time and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough; the hour has come. The Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.

42Get up, let us go. The one who hands Me over has come near."

The Arrest

43At once, while He was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.

44The one handing Him over had given them a signal, saying, "The one I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away under guard."

45When he came, he went up to Him at once and said, "Rabbi!" and kissed Him.

46They laid hands on Him and arrested Him.

47But one of those standing by drew his sword, struck the high priest's slave and cut off his ear.

48Jesus said to them, "Have you come out with swords and clubs to seize Me as if I were a robber?

49Day after day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not arrest Me. But this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled."

50They all left Him and fled.

51A young man was following Him, wearing nothing but a linen cloth over his naked body; they seized him,

52but he left the linen cloth and fled naked.

Before the Council

53They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes gathered.

54Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the guards and warming himself at the fire.

55The chief priests and the whole council were looking for testimony against Jesus so that they might put Him to death, but they found none.

56For many gave false testimony against Him, but their testimony did not agree.

57Some stood up and gave false testimony against Him, saying,

58"We heard Him say, 'I will destroy this sanctuary made with hands, and in three days I will build another not made with hands.'"

59Even so their testimony did not agree.

60The high priest stood up in the middle and asked Jesus, "Have You no answer? What is it that these men testify against You?"

61But He was silent and made no answer. Again the high priest asked Him, "Are You the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One?"

62Jesus said, "I am; and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven."

63The high priest tore his clothes and said, "What further need do we have of witnesses?

64You have heard the blasphemy. What do you think?" They all condemned Him as deserving death.

65Some began to spit on Him, to cover His face and strike Him with their fists, and to say to Him, "Prophesy!" The guards took Him and slapped Him.

Peter's Denial

66While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest's servant girls came,

67and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, "You also were with the Nazarene, Jesus."

68But he denied it, saying, "I do not know or understand what you are talking about." He went out into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.

69The servant girl saw him and began again to say to those standing by, "This man is one of them."

70But again he denied it. After a little while those standing by said to Peter again, "Surely you are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech is like theirs."

71But he began to call down curses and to swear, "I do not know this man you are talking about."

72At once a rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered the word Jesus had said to him: "Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times." He broke down and wept.

Notes

  • vv3–9 "an alabaster jar of perfume, pure nard… poured it on His head… anointed My body beforehand for burial" — nardou pistikēs, pure nard; pistikēs is obscure, perhaps genuine. A king's head was anointed, as Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head (1 Samuel 10:1); Jesus says it is for His burial. Three hundred denarii is near a year's wages (Matthew 20:2). The good news is preached in the whole world, as 13:10.

  • vv12–16 "when they sacrificed the Passover lamb… a man carrying a jar of water… a large upper room" — to pascha ethyon, they sacrificed the Passover, the lamb of Exodus 12. Kataluma, guest room.

  • vv17–21 "one who is eating with Me… dipping bread into the bowl with Me" — the psalm, Even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted up his heel against me (Psalm 41:9). Mēti egō, Surely not I?, a question that expects No.

  • vv22–25 "this is My body… This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many" — to haima mou tēs diathēkēs, My blood of the covenant, the words of Moses at Sinai, Here is the blood of the covenant (Exodus 24:8; the note on Matthew 26:28). Hyper pollōn, for many, as in 10:45. Mark has no for the forgiveness of sins (Matthew 26:28).

  • vv26–31 "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered… before a rooster crows twice" — Zechariah 13:7, Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, here in the first person, I will strike. Only Mark has twice (vv30, 72), and the rooster crows at v68 and v72.

  • vv32–42 "Abba, Father… Take this cup away from Me… the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak" — Abba is Aramaic, Father, and Mark gives it with its meaning. Ekthambeisthai kai adēmonein, greatly distressed and troubled. Perilypos… heōs thanatou, deeply grieved, to the point of death, as the psalm, Why are you bowed down, my soul? (Psalm 42:5). The cup of 10:38. Apechei, It is enough, is obscure, perhaps it is settled.

  • vv43–52 "swords and clubs… The one I kiss is the man… a young man… fled naked" — katephilēsen, kissed, a strong form of the word in v44. Only Mark has the young man, who leaves his sindōn, linen cloth, the word for the cloth Jesus will be buried in (15:46). All flee, as 14:27 said.

  • vv53–65 "this sanctuary made with hands… Are You the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One?… I am" — ho eulogētos, the Blessed One, a way of naming God without saying the word. Egō eimi, I am, Jesus' plain answer in Mark, where Matthew has You have said it (Matthew 26:64). The answer joins Psalm 110:1, Sit at My right hand (12:36), and Daniel 7:13, with the clouds of heaven. Prophēteuson, Prophesy!, mocked while His word to Peter comes true below.

  • vv66–72 "below in the courtyard… a Galilean, and your speech is like theirs… He broke down and wept" — Mark sets Peter's denial at the same time as the trial (v54): Jesus confesses, Peter denies. Hē lalia sou homoiazei, your speech is like theirs: the edition reads these words and marks them as a place where manuscripts differ. Anathematizein, to call down curses. Epibalōn eklaien, He broke down and wept: epibalōn is obscure, word for word having thrown on.

chapters.title: The King of the Jews
chapters.html:
Mark 15

Before Pilate

1At once, early in the morning, the chief priests with the elders and scribes and the whole council held a consultation. They bound Jesus, led Him away and handed Him over to Pilate.

2Pilate asked Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?" He answered him, "You say so."

3The chief priests accused Him of many things.

4Pilate asked Him again, "Have You no answer? See how many things they accuse You of."

5But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate was amazed.

6At the feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whomever they asked for.

7There was one called Barabbas, in prison with the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising.

8The crowd came up and began to ask him to do as he usually did for them.

9Pilate answered them, "Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?"

10For he knew that it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Him over.

11But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas for them instead.

12Pilate answered them again, "Then what shall I do with the one you call the King of the Jews?"

13They shouted back, "Crucify Him!"

14Pilate said to them, "Why, what evil has He done?" But they shouted all the more, "Crucify Him!"

15So Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them; and after having Jesus flogged, he handed Him over to be crucified.

The Soldiers' Mockery

16The soldiers led Him away into the courtyard, that is, the governor's headquarters, and called together the whole cohort.

17They dressed Him in purple, twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on Him,

18and they began to salute Him: "Hail, King of the Jews!"

19They struck His head with a reed and spat on Him, and kneeling down they paid homage to Him.

20When they had mocked Him, they stripped Him of the purple and put His own clothes on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.

The Crucifixion

21They forced a passer-by, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, who was coming in from the country, to carry His cross.

22They brought Him to the place called Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull.

23They offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.

24They crucified Him and divided His clothes among them, casting lots for them to decide what each should take.

25It was the third hour when they crucified Him.

26The inscription of the charge against Him read, "The King of the Jews."

27With Him they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.

29Those who passed by blasphemed Him, shaking their heads and saying, "Aha! You who would destroy the sanctuary and build it in three days,

30save Yourself, and come down from the cross!"

31In the same way the chief priests also, with the scribes, mocked Him among themselves and said, "He saved others; He cannot save Himself.

32Let the Messiah, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe." Those who were crucified with Him also taunted Him.

33When the sixth hour came, there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.

34At the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" which means, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?"

35Some of those standing by, when they heard it, said, "Listen, He is calling Elijah."

36Someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed and gave it to Him to drink, saying, "Wait, let us see whether Elijah comes to take Him down."

37Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.

38The curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two, from top to bottom.

39When the centurion who stood facing Him saw that He breathed His last in this way, he said, "Truly this man was the Son of God!"

40There were also women watching from a distance; among them were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.

41When He was in Galilee, they used to follow Him and serve Him; and there were many other women who had come up with Him to Jerusalem.

The Burial

42When evening had already come, since it was the day of Preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,

43Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council, who was himself waiting for the kingdom of God, came and went boldly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

44Pilate was amazed that He was already dead; and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether He had been dead long.

45When he learned it from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

46Joseph bought a linen cloth, took Him down, wrapped Him in the linen cloth and laid Him in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock; and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.

47Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where He was laid.

Notes

  • vv1–5 "early in the morning… Are You the King of the Jews?… You say so… made no further answer" — prōi, early in the morning, the last watch of 13:35. Ho basileus tōn Ioudaiōn, the King of the Jews, six times in the chapter (vv2, 9, 12, 18, 26; King of Israel, v32): the charge is that He is a king. His silence is the servant's, he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter (Isaiah 53:7).

  • vv6–15 "Barabbas… the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising… Crucify Him!" — Barabbas, son of a father, bar abba, as Jesus prays Abba (14:36). Stasiastai, rebels, and stasis, uprising. Phragellōsas, having Him flogged, a word borrowed from Latin.

  • vv16–20 "the governor's headquarters… the whole cohort… purple… a crown of thorns… Hail, King of the Jews!" — praitōrion, the governor's headquarters, a word borrowed from Latin, as is speira, cohort, a unit of soldiers. Porphyra, purple, the color of kings; Matthew has a scarlet cloak (Matthew 27:28). Prosekynoun, paid homage, the word of 5:6: the soldiers do in mockery what the possessed man did in truth.

  • vv21–27 "Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus… wine mixed with myrrh… casting lots… the third hour" — only Mark names Simon's sons. Esmyrnismenon oinon, wine mixed with myrrh; Matthew has gall (Matthew 27:34). The lots are the psalm's, they divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots (Psalm 22:18). v28 is not in the edition, so the numbering here skips from 27 to 29.

  • vv29–32 "shaking their heads… Aha!… He saved others; He cannot save Himself" — the psalm again, they make mouths at me; they shake their heads (Psalm 22:7). Oua, Aha!, a cry of scorn, found only here. Esōsen… sōsai, saved… save: the mockers speak the truth without knowing it. Two robbers, one on each side, where James and John asked to sit (10:37, 40).

  • vv33–37 "darkness over all the land… Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?… sour wine… breathed His last" — the darkness of Amos, I will make the sun go down at noon (Amos 8:9). Eloi is the Aramaic form; Matthew has Eli (Matthew 27:46). The words are the first line of Psalm 22, My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? Oxos, sour wine, as for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink (Psalm 69:21). Exepneusen, breathed His last, word for word breathed out.

  • vv38–39 "The curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two… Truly this man was the Son of God!" — eschisthē, was torn, the verb of the heavens torn open at the baptism (1:10): at the beginning and the end, a voice or a witness says Son. The curtain hung before the Holy of Holies, The veil shall divide for you between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies (Exodus 26:33). Kentyriōn, centurion, a word borrowed from Latin, an officer over a hundred. He is the first in Mark, apart from the unclean spirits (3:11; 5:7), to call Him Son of God. Huios theou has no article: the Son of God, or a son of God.

  • vv40–47 "women watching from a distance… the day of Preparation… Joseph of Arimathea… a tomb that had been cut out of the rock" — the women who followed and served Him, as disciples do (1:18, 31). Paraskeuē, Preparation, and prosabbaton, the day before the sabbath: the law did not allow a hanged body to stay overnight (Deuteronomy 21:22–23). Euschēmōn bouleutēs, a respected member of the council. Ptōma, corpse, the word used of John's body (6:29). Sindōn, linen cloth, the cloth the young man left behind (14:51–52).

speech.text: Mark 15
Before Pilate
At once, early in the morning, the chief priests with the elders and scribes and the whole council held a consultation. They bound Jesus, led Him away and handed Him over to Pilate.
Pilate asked Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?" He answered him, "You say so."
The chief priests accused Him of many things.
Pilate asked Him again, "Have You no answer? See how many things they accuse You of."
But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate was amazed.
At the feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whomever they asked for.
There was one called Barabbas, in prison with the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising.
The crowd came up and began to ask him to do as he usually did for them.
Pilate answered them, "Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?"
For he knew that it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Him over.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas for them instead.
Pilate answered them again, "Then what shall I do with the one you call the King of the Jews?"
They shouted back, "Crucify Him!"
Pilate said to them, "Why, what evil has He done?" But they shouted all the more, "Crucify Him!"
So Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them; and after having Jesus flogged, he handed Him over to be crucified.
The Soldiers' Mockery
The soldiers led Him away into the courtyard, that is, the governor's headquarters, and called together the whole cohort.
They dressed Him in purple, twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on Him,
and they began to salute Him: "Hail, King of the Jews!"
They struck His head with a reed and spat on Him, and kneeling down they paid homage to Him.
When they had mocked Him, they stripped Him of the purple and put His own clothes on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.
The Crucifixion
They forced a passer-by, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, who was coming in from the country, to carry His cross.
They brought Him to the place called Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull.
They offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
They crucified Him and divided His clothes among them, casting lots for them to decide what each should take.
It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
The inscription of the charge against Him read, "The King of the Jews."
With Him they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
Those who passed by blasphemed Him, shaking their heads and saying, "Aha! You who would destroy the sanctuary and build it in three days,
save Yourself, and come down from the cross!"
In the same way the chief priests also, with the scribes, mocked Him among themselves and said, "He saved others; He cannot save Himself.
Let the Messiah, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe." Those who were crucified with Him also taunted Him.
When the sixth hour came, there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" which means, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?"
Some of those standing by, when they heard it, said, "Listen, He is calling Elijah."
Someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed and gave it to Him to drink, saying, "Wait, let us see whether Elijah comes to take Him down."
Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
The curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two, from top to bottom.
When the centurion who stood facing Him saw that He breathed His last in this way, he said, "Truly this man was the Son of God!"
There were also women watching from a distance; among them were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
When He was in Galilee, they used to follow Him and serve Him; and there were many other women who had come up with Him to Jerusalem.
The Burial
When evening had already come, since it was the day of Preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council, who was himself waiting for the kingdom of God, came and went boldly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Pilate was amazed that He was already dead; and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether He had been dead long.
When he learned it from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.
Joseph bought a linen cloth, took Him down, wrapped Him in the linen cloth and laid Him in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock; and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where He was laid.

chapters.title: He Has Been Raised
chapters.html:
Mark 16

The Empty Tomb

1When the sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices, so that they might go and anoint Him.

2Very early on the first day of the week, when the sun had risen, they went to the tomb.

3They were saying to one another, "Who will roll away the stone for us from the door of the tomb?"

4Looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled back; for it was very large.

5Going into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe, and they were greatly alarmed.

6He said to them, "Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has been raised; He is not here. See the place where they laid Him.

7But go, tell His disciples and Peter, 'He is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see Him, just as He told you.'"

8They went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and amazement had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.

The Shorter Ending

They reported briefly to those around Peter all that they had been told. After this Jesus Himself sent out through them, from the east to the west, the holy and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.

The Longer Ending

9When He had risen early on the first day of the week, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons.

10She went and told those who had been with Him, as they mourned and wept.

11When they heard that He was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe it.

12After this He appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking into the country.

13They went back and told the rest, but they did not believe them either.

14Later He appeared to the eleven themselves as they were reclining at table, and He reproached them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen Him after He had been raised.

15He said to them, "Go into all the world and preach the good news to all creation.

16Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.

17These signs will accompany those who believe: in My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues;

18they will pick up snakes, and if they drink anything deadly, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will recover."

19So the Lord Jesus, after He had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.

20They went out and preached everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word through the signs that accompanied it.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "When the sabbath was over… spices… Who will roll away the stone for us?" — diagenomenou tou sabbatou, when the sabbath was over, at sunset, when buying was allowed again. Tē mia tōn sabbatōn, the first day of the week, word for word the one of the sabbaths. The large stone was the one Joseph rolled against the door (15:46).

  • vv5–7 "a young man… in a white robe… He has been raised; He is not here… tell His disciples and Peter" — neaniskos, a young man, the word of the one who fled in 14:51; Matthew has an angel of the Lord (Matthew 28:2). Ēgerthē, He has been raised, the verb of 1:31 and 5:41. And Peter, named apart, the one who denied Him (14:72). Proagei, He is going ahead, as He promised in 14:28.

  • v8 "they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid" — ephobounto gar, for they were afraid: the Greek sentence ends on gar, for. Matthew has with fear and great joy, and ran to tell His disciples (Matthew 28:8).

  • The shorter ending — the edition prints it after v8 inside double brackets, as it does vv9–20; it has no verse number. From the east to the west, the words of Malachi 1:11, from the rising of the sun to its setting.

  • vv9–20, the longer ending — the edition prints these verses inside double brackets, as it does the shorter ending.

  • vv9–14 "He appeared first to Mary Magdalene… in another form to two of them… the eleven" — Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons: the earlier chapters of Mark do not tell of this. Eleven: the twelve without Judas. Sklērokardia, hardness of heart, the word of 10:5.

  • vv15–20 "preach the good news to all creation… taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God" — the good news… to all the nations (13:10). Anelēmphthē, was taken up, the verb the Greek of 2 Kings uses of Elijah, who went up in a whirlwind to heaven (2 Kings 2:11). At the right hand of God, Psalm 110:1, Sit at My right hand (12:36; 14:62).
